probes.text: A British officer serving with UN peacekeepers on the Turkey–Syria border is abruptly summoned home to England.
A wealthy outside investor tours the grand country estate, taking a keen interest in its cellar of vintage wine.
Eddie is driven out to visit Susie's father, held in an oddly luxurious open-air prison.
Eddie, in black tie and clearly not enjoying himself, attends a lavish gala hosted by Johnston.
Eddie sneaks into a chop shop at night, tasked with stealing a Lamborghini Huracan from among the dismantled cars.
Susie takes on a favour for an Albanian gang boss annoyed that his weed shipment has not arrived.
Eddie's mother frets about the family's slide into criminality, while Susie remarks how calm he stays under fire.
Jimmy, thoroughly smitten, gives Gabrielle a proud personal tour around the underground farm.
Eddie and Susie drive out to a Travellers' camp to speak with the family's leader about two missing generators.
Two generators vanish from the weed farm, and Susie needs Eddie's help sorting out who took them.
The Belgian who runs the shipping side of the Glass distribution starts pushing for a bigger cut.
At a glitzy boxing party, Eddie falls into conversation with a smooth ex-army officer who promotes fighters.
Susie tells Eddie the money still needs another three months of laundering before it counts as clean profit.
Eddie and Freddy pay a call on an ageing lord, a former associate of the Glasses, at his crumbling pile.

8.title: The Gospel According to Bobby Glass

probes.text: Lady Sabrina adds her own quiet encouragement when Susie is hesitating, pressing her gently rather than arguing.

fine_only.text: Armed Glass men arrive in numbers at Halstead Manor and take up positions around the house and grounds.
